lookAt: Incident and near-miss records from the last 3 months and what was done after each one
Minutes or notes showing lessons shared with the team
Any themes found across incidents and how they were tackled
askPeople: If something went wrong with your care, were you told and did anything change?
Do you feel able to raise a worry about your safety?
askStaff: Tell me about a recent incident. What changed because of it?
How do you hear about lessons learned from other carers' incidents?
inCareFlow: Incidents: open and closed incidents, actions and lessons

lookAt: Hospital discharge and admission records for 2 or 3 people
How information is handed over to and from GPs, district nurses and hospitals
How a new package of care is started safely
askPeople: When you came home from hospital, did your care start on time and did carers know what had changed?

Visits: first visits after a discharge

lookAt: Safeguarding log, referrals made to the local authority and their outcomes
Safeguarding training records for all staff
Mental Capacity Act and any Deprivation of Liberty (or Court of Protection) paperwork
askPeople: Do you feel safe with your carers?
Who would you tell if a carer treated you badly?
askStaff: What would you do if you thought someone was being abused or neglected?
Who is the safeguarding lead and how do you contact them out of hours?

lookAt: Risk assessments for 3 or 4 people (falls, moving and handling, skin, choking, home environment)

lookAt: Home environment risk assessments (access, key safes, fire, trip hazards)
Equipment checks (hoists, slings, bed rails) and who services them
Lone working arrangements for carers
askPeople: Is the equipment you use checked and working?
askStaff: What do you check when you arrive at a person's home?
How do you report broken equipment?
inCareFlow: Service users: home and access details

lookAt: Rotas, travel time and visit times against what was planned
Missed and late visit records and why they happened
Recruitment files for 3 recent starters (DBS, references, right to work, gaps in work history)
Induction, the Care Certificate and mandatory training
askPeople: Do carers arrive on time and stay for the full visit?
Do you usually see the same carers?
askStaff: Do you get enough travel time between visits?
What training did you have before you started visiting people alone?
inCareFlow: Visits: punctuality, missed and late visits

PPE supply and how carers get it
Hand hygiene and IPC training records, and any outbreak records

askStaff: How do you get PPE and what do you do if you run out?
What would you do if you or a person you support had an infection?

lookAt: Medication administration records (MAR) for 3 or 4 people over the last month: gaps, errors, PRN notes

Do carers explain what they are giving you?

lookAt: Initial assessments and care plans for 3 or 4 people

askPeople: Were you asked what support you need and how you like things done?
Has anyone checked recently whether your care still suits you?
askStaff: Where do you find out about a new person's needs before your first visit?
inCareFlow: Service users: initial assessments, care plans and review dates

lookAt: Whether care follows current good practice (for example NICE guidance for home care, pressure care, nutrition)
Policies and procedures and when they were last reviewed
Specialist plans (diabetes, epilepsy, catheter, PEG) and the training for them
askPeople: Do carers know how to help with your health conditions?
askStaff: How do you keep up to date with good practice?
Which specialist care have you been trained to give?

lookAt: Records of contact with GPs, district nurses, social workers and families
How information is shared between carers who visit the same person
Handovers and communication notes
askPeople: Do your carers know what other carers did on earlier visits?
askStaff: How do you pass on something important to the next carer?
How do you work with district nurses or the GP?

lookAt: Nutrition and hydration plans and records for people at risk
How carers spot and report changes in health (weight, skin, mood, eating)
Support with health appointments and healthy routines
askPeople: Do carers help you eat, drink and stay well in the way you want?
askStaff: What would you do if you noticed someone was not eating or drinking?

lookAt: How the service checks that care is making a difference (reviews, outcomes, feedback)
Audits of care records and what was done about the findings
Trends in falls, pressure damage, hospital admissions or missed visits
askPeople: Has your care helped you do the things that matter to you?
askStaff: How do you know your care is working for someone?

lookAt: Consent to care records and who signed them
Mental capacity assessments and best-interest decisions where people cannot consent
Lasting power of attorney details checked and recorded
askPeople: Do carers ask before they help you?
askStaff: What does the Mental Capacity Act mean in your daily work?
What do you do if someone says no to care?
inCareFlow: Service users: consent and capacity records, representatives

lookAt: Compliments and complaints about how people are treated
Survey results about respect and dignity
Spot checks and observations of care
askPeople: Are your carers kind and respectful?
Do they protect your privacy, for example during personal care?
askStaff: How do you protect someone's dignity during personal care?

lookAt: Care plans that describe the person: history, likes, culture, faith, language
How people's equality and diversity needs are met
askPeople: Do your carers know you as a person and what matters to you?
askStaff: Tell me about the person you are visiting next. What matters to them?
inCareFlow: Service users: personal profile and care plan

lookAt: Care plans that say what people can do for themselves
Records showing people's choices are followed (times, carers, routines)
askPeople: Do carers let you do things for yourself and make your own choices?
Can you choose the time of your visits or ask for a different carer?
askStaff: How do you help someone stay as independent as possible?

lookAt: How urgent requests and worries during visits are handled
On-call and out-of-hours records
What carers do when a person is unwell, in pain or distressed
askPeople: If you need help quickly, does someone respond?
askStaff: What do you do if a person is in pain or upset when you arrive?
Is the on-call manager easy to reach?

lookAt: Supervision and appraisal records
Staff survey results and what was done
Support for staff wellbeing (sickness, stress, lone working, after an incident)
askStaff: Do you feel supported and valued by managers?
When did you last have supervision?

lookAt: Care plans written with the person, in their words where possible
Whether care changes when the person's wishes or needs change
askPeople: Were you involved in writing your care plan?
Does your care fit around your life?
askStaff: How do you find out how a person likes their care done?
inCareFlow: Service users: care plans and reviews

lookAt: How many different carers each person sees in a month
Planned versus actual visit times, and visit cancellations
Joint working when people use other services
askPeople: Do you know which carer is coming?
Are you told if a carer is running late?
askStaff: Do you usually visit the same people?

lookAt: Information given to people (service guide, rota, how to complain) and its formats
Accessible Information Standard: communication needs recorded and met
askPeople: Do you get information in a way you can understand?
Do you know who to call at the office?
askStaff: How do you support someone who has difficulty communicating?

lookAt: Complaints log: response times, outcomes and lessons
Surveys and other feedback, and 'You said, we did' actions
askPeople: Do you know how to complain?
If you raised a concern, were you listened to?
askStaff: What do you do if someone tells you they are unhappy with their care?
inCareFlow: Surveys: actions and 'You said, we did'

lookAt: How the service makes sure everyone can get the care they need, whatever their background, disability or where they live

askPeople: Has anything made it harder for you to get the care you need?
askStaff: How would you support someone whose first language is not English?
inCareFlow: Service users: language and communication needs

lookAt: Whether outcomes and feedback differ between groups of people and what is done about it

askPeople: Do you feel you are treated fairly?
askStaff: How do you make sure people with different needs get equally good care?
inCareFlow: Surveys: results by group (where numbers allow)

lookAt: Advance care plans and end of life wishes (including DNACPR / ReSPECT where relevant)

askStaff: How do you support someone at the end of their life and their family?

lookAt: The service's vision and values and how staff know them
Business plan or service improvement plan
askPeople: Do you know who runs the service?
askStaff: What are the service's values and how do they show in your work?
inCareFlow: Policies: values and statement of purpose

lookAt: The registered manager's registration, training and how visible they are
Leadership structure and cover when the manager is away
Statutory notifications sent to CQC
askPeople: Do you know the manager? Is the office helpful?
askStaff: Is the manager approachable? Do they act on what you tell them?

lookAt: Whistleblowing policy and records of concerns raised by staff
How staff concerns were handled and fed back
askStaff: Would you feel safe raising a concern, even about a manager?
Do you know how to whistleblow outside the organisation?

lookAt: Equality and diversity policy and training
How fair recruitment, pay, training and promotion are checked
askStaff: Are all staff treated fairly here?

lookAt: The audit programme (care plans, MAR, visits, files) and actions from audits

Key performance data (missed visits, incidents, complaints, training) and how it is used

askStaff: What audits do you take part in and what changed because of them?

lookAt: Work with the local authority, commissioners, health services and community groups
Feedback from partners and professionals
askStaff: Which other services do you work with most?

lookAt: The service improvement plan and progress against it
How learning from feedback, audits, incidents and inspections leads to change

lookAt: Steps taken to reduce the service's impact on the environment (travel, paper, waste)
